executive_assessment.text: Named provinces and regions face different agricultural, road, water and coastal livelihood pressures. Acosta offers one dated storm-isolation and community-recovery case.
The 2026 NAP progress review identifies implementation and finance gaps, but its product-coverage figures require reconciliation and do not establish adaptation outcomes.
Water-user conflict prevention near Nicoya, Indigenous family farming, Huetar Norte farms and Paquera-Tambor fisheries are project designs in an undated registry, not delivered or evaluated effects.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2025-07 reports: In 1980–2017, events were most frequent in Limón, Puntarenas and Alajuela; 72% were heavy rain, storms or hail.
Source dated 2025-07 reports: Chorotega droughts primarily affect agriculture; extreme rain mainly impacts roads, farms and homes.
Source dated 2025-07 reports: Huetar Caribe extreme rainfall mainly affects roads, farms, rivers and streams; cited risks also include farm and fishing yields.
Source dated 2024-06-28 reports: After October 2017 Storm Nate, about 20,000 Acosta residents were cut off for days without water, electricity, food or medicine.
Source dated 2024-06-28 reports: Acosta residents organized food/medicine delivery and recovery planning; over 400 participated, helping inspire 32 municipalities to join an SDG network.
Source dated 2026 reports: A planned automated groundwater network for Central and Huetar Norte was to track water levels, temperature and conductivity, but its progress was unreported.

The undated MINAE project registry describes intended family-farming and food-security adaptation with Bribri and Cabécar organizations associated with Talamanca and Valle de la Estrella. Named territories are not assumed to be the same administrative unit; delivery and outcomes are unverified.

MINAE's undated registry lists a Nicoya/Hojancha/Nandayure water project intended to reduce water-use conflict and future disputes under increasing water deficit. This documents a design objective, not observed conflict, an actual prevention effect or current project status.
Source dated not stated reports: A Huetar Norte program lists 36-month adaptation support on 60 farms for soil/water conservation, crop diversity and water harvesting.
Source dated not stated reports: A Paquera-Tambor project proposes coastal-ecosystem protection and climate-adaptation capacity-building with fisher associations.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 16 of 16 evidence records and 0 of 0 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
CRI has no baseline dossier in EXISTING_COUNTRIES.json or countries/CRI in this worktree; this is a new-country extraction.

The only explicit climate-to-conflict pathway located is a MINAE project objective concerning water-use conflict and rising water deficit near Nicoya; the register does not establish observed conflict or project effectiveness.
The IACHR reports Indigenous land occupation and violence, but the inspected chapter does not connect those events to climate hazards or adaptation; no such link is inferred.
No inspected primary source states that violence or insecurity interrupted climate adaptation or disaster response in Costa Rica.

Regional event records summarized in the Adaptation Fund proposal end in 2017 and are not a current, climate-attributed exposure inventory; several regional risk statements lack scenario and household-level estimates.
The 2026 NAP progress review covered 179 of 232 products; 56 had no progress information and 43 were unstarted or canceled, limiting assessment of implementation outcomes.

A project objective links increasing water deficit with intended prevention of water-use conflict near Nicoya. It does not establish an observed conflict mechanism or evaluated peace outcome; no full pathway is forced.
Indigenous land violence is documented elsewhere, but no inspected passage connects it to climate hazards or adaptation interruption. These issues are not causally joined.
The NAP report's coverage figures are internally ambiguous: 179 products reportedly covered differs from 232 minus 56 unknown. Status tallies are implementation reporting, not resilience impacts.
The regional proposal relies on older records and secondary government analyses; a Brunca risk projection without a source-stated period was excluded.
The undated project registry gives aims and durations, not verified current delivery or completed outcomes. Geographic references to Talamanca and Valle de la Estrella are not conflated.
Routine/default app-use approval granted by Lindsey Jones on 2026-10-27; independent source verification remains incomplete. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
